_note: The character is pinned to the trap, so the trap is the fixed point and the anchor: pivot "ground" centres each frame on whatever is standing on the floor. Anchoring on the torso, which is right for a walk, swings the trap 40px either way here and reads as the mouse dragging the trap around rather than being held.
_sizeNote: Bigger, emptier frame than the walk sheet on purpose. Measured off the strips, a trapped pose reaches 160px either side of the trap and 230px above it; at the walk sheet's 256px frame that clipped 14 of the 32 frames. The character itself is scaled identically to the walk sheet — metadata carries charHeight so the renderer sizes by the character rather than by the frame.
_renderScaleNote: Same as the cat. renderScale comes from head width, not silhouette height.
_trapNote: The trap in these strips was regenerated larger. The first set drew it at 12-14px at the game cell size, under paint.js's own 22px rule for a hazard and a third of the 37px vector trap, so a sprung trap looked smaller than the ones you walked past. It now measures 26-36px. The instruction that produced it states the base plate as a fraction of the character's height — 0.55 for the cat, 0.85 for the mouse — because "bigger" on its own moved it only a third of the way.
